conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Circuit Board
style.description: A macro photograph of a real printed circuit board: deep matte-satin solder mask over copper pours, glossy gold traces and pads, white silkscreen lettering, black chips with gull-wing pin rows, tiny resistors, capacitors and LEDs, shallow depth of field and one low raking light. Signals travel as bright pulses along octilinear traces through vias; each part powers up when a pulse reaches it (LED lights, chip label glows, a silkscreen caption prints itself) while the camera tracks the pulse at macro scale.
motion: A signal is a bright pulse with a short comet tail running along an exposed trace at constant speed; behind it the trace keeps a faint powered glow.
Traces are octilinear (0/45/90°) with 45° chamfered corners; a via flashes as the pulse dives through it.
When a pulse reaches a part it powers up: an LED lights and spills colour on the mask, a chip's silkscreen-style label glows, and a small silkscreen caption prints itself left to right.
The camera is a macro lens: shallow depth of field, low angle, tracking the pulse across the board and settling on each part as it powers up; a final pull-back shows the whole lit path.

objects.procedural: dark matte work surface 0.51 m below the board top (out of focus)

scene.notes: Board, parts, traces, pulses and captions are built in scene.js from circuit-board props; layout, routes, pulse plan, camera keys and SCORE come from signals.js. Neutral idea, no numbers, no brands.
